text:
Erin: Observing persistent KV residency drift on multi-tenant nodes during prolonged generation. Node kube-kv-7 grew from ~40% to ~87% over ~5h, causing eviction churn affecting tenant-beta.
Erin: Repro steps: burst 64 concurrent sessions, ctx length ~120k tokens, model redwood-xl-int8, continuous batching enabled, new kernel selector active. No OOM but eviction churn.
Erin: Log excerpt:
```
[11:08:02] KV: pin page tenant=tenant-beta addr=0x7f... refs=15
[11:08:03] KV: tenant_resident=142MB tenant=tenant-beta
[11:08:04] KV: eviction triggered victim=tenant-alpha pages=30 cause=soft_limit
[11:08:05] KV: pagewalk latency=10.8ms
```
Raj: Are there perf traces for kernel selection + kv_pagewalk? Might show where refs are held.
Erin: Uploaded perf svg to ticket #INC-4212. Flamegraph shows hot stacks in kv_pagewalk and kernel_choose_path; new matmul path shows deeper stack and longer spans holding page refs.
bot: telemetry-alert: kv_residency_growth node=kube-kv-7 avg+8.5MB/min over 5h. @Erin @Sam
Gina: Hypothesis: the kernel path chosen for long attention requires synchronous KV access (holds pins) rather than streaming; that increases per-session resident set and reduces reuse.
Sam: Microbench on dev: 128 sessions longctx
- legacy-kernel: ~52MB/session, reuse~=70%
- kernel-v2: ~81MB/session, reuse~=40%, fragmentation up
Command:
./kv_stress --tenants=3 --sessions=128 --ctx=120000 --kernels=legacy,kernel-v2 --out=./out
Gina: Lower reuse + higher residency gives noisy neighbors eviction wins.
Raj: Short-term mitigations:
- lower per-tenant soft watermark (config flip)
- pin kernel to legacy for longctx via routing rule
- implement LRU-like eviction across tenants with hysteresis
Erin: Can we flip soft-watermark to 0.6 of quota on a staging pool and monitor p99 latency and eviction freq?
Sam: Deployed soft-watermark flag (--kv-soft-watermark=0.6) to staging nodes staging-kv-{a,b}. Preliminary: eviction events down ~70%, victim p99 latency improved ~20%. Still collecting 24h traces.
Gina: For long-term: make kernel path stream KV asynchronously, or add a cooperative compaction that groups hot pages and frees fragments, or per-tenant hard caps with warm-up allowances.
Raj: Requesting better metrics: per-tenant page-age histogram, fragmentation index, reuse-hit-rate. That will let us correlate kernel path with fragmentation.
Erin: I'll file tracking ticket for kernels + runtime to (1) add telemetry (per-tenant page-age, fragmentation, reuse rates), (2) prototype async-streaming kernel variant, (3) evaluate per-tenant caps on subset capacity. Linking ticket when created.
Sam: I'll keep the staging flip live and add the reproduction script to eng-runtime CI. Will attach profiles and traces to ticket.
Gina: If we adopt per-tenant hard caps, need migration plan: offer gradual warm-up or bump policy so large customers won't be disrupted.
Erin: Agreed. For immediate ops: maintain soft-watermark on staging and monitor cluster-wide. Reopen if regressions.
Raj: Thanks — please post any regression flags. Also include a note if any unrelated workload latency moves after config flip.
Sam: Ping me for the repro script; I'll drop it in eng-runtime repo and CI.
Erin: Closing for now; will post ticket links + graphs here once available. :thumbsup:
